root_cause.text: In Bluetooth L2CAP's l2cap_ecred_conn_req(), rsp_len was derived from attacker-controlled cmd_len before validating num_scid against L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID, so oversized Enhanced Credit Based Connection Requests caused l2cap_send_cmd() to read past the fixed-size 18-byte stack pdu buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `rsp_len = cmd_len;` from before `if (num_scid > L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID) { ... goto response; }` to after that check, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that with more than 5 SCIDs the function jumped to `response` while retaining an oversized `rsp_len`, leading to a stack-out-of-bounds read of `pdu` in `l2cap_build_cmd()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move response-length initialization after SCID-count validation so invalid ECRED requests do not use an unchecked request-based response length.
intent_record.what: The assignment `rsp_len = cmd_len;` and its accompanying comment were moved from before the `if (num_scid > L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID)` check to after that validation block, with no other code changes in the hunk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `rsp_len` is no longer set when the request contains too many SCIDs and execution jumps to `response`; this avoids using the request-derived response length on the invalid-parameter path and limits that assignment to validated input.

grouping_result.intent: Move response-length initialization after SCID-count validation so invalid ECRED requests do not use an unchecked request-based response length.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by delaying rsp_len calculation until after validating num_scid, preventing attacker-controlled cmd_len from influencing the response length for invalid ECRED requests and avoiding the out-of-bounds read from the fixed-size pdu buffer.

candidates.rationale: This directly assigns the response length from attacker-controlled cmd_len before validating num_scid against L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID, enabling an oversized response length that later causes l2cap_send_cmd() to read past the fixed-size stack pdu buffer.

This derives the SCID count from attacker-controlled cmd_len, and its result is only checked after rsp_len has already been set from cmd_len, contributing to the ordering flaw behind the out-of-bounds read.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assigns the response length directly from attacker-controlled cmd_len before validating num_scid against L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID. As a result, invalid oversized ECRED requests can cause l2cap_send_cmd() to use an excessive length and read past the fixed-size 18-byte stack pdu buffer.

This derives num_scid from attacker-controlled cmd_len, and the validation of that derived count happens only after rsp_len has already been set from cmd_len. It is part of the flawed ordering that allowed an unchecked oversized response length to persist.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix result of L2CAP_ECRED_CONN_RSP when MTU is too short

Test L2CAP/ECFC/BV-26-C expect the response
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit c28d2bff70444a85b3b86aaf241ece9408c7858c
Author: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Date:   Thu Feb 5 15:11:34 2026 -0500

    Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix result of L2CAP_ECRED_CONN_RSP when MTU is too short
    
    Test L2CAP/ECFC/BV-26-C expect the response to L2CAP_ECRED_CONN_REQ with
    and MTU value < L2CAP_ECRED_MIN_MTU (64) to be L2CAP_CR_LE_INVALID_PARAMS
    rather than L2CAP_CR_LE_UNACCEPT_PARAMS.
    
    Also fix not including the correct number of CIDs in the respo
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the full relevant control flow in l2cap_ecred_conn_req() around how the response length is computed and validated. The vulnerable construct is present: after `cmd_len -= sizeof(*req); num_scid = cmd_len / sizeof(u16);`, the code immediately does `rsp_len = cmd_len;` with the comment `/* Always respond with the same number of scids as in the request */`. Only after that does it validate `if (num_scid > L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID) { result = L2CAP_CR_LE_INVALID_PARAMS; goto response; }`. At the end, the function sends `l2cap_send_cmd(..., sizeof(*pdu) + rsp_len, pdu);`. Since `rsp_len` is derived directly from attacker-controlled `cmd_len` before checking `num_scid` against `L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID`, an oversized request can cause the response length to exceed the fixed stack `pdu` buffer size, matching the root cause. Nothing in this commit fixes that ordering or caps `rsp_len` before the `goto response` path. The changes shown only add `memset(pdu, 0, sizeof(*pdu))`, change the MTU-too-short result code, and switch from `len` accumulated during iteration to `rsp_len = cmd_len`, which still remains attacker-controlled prior to bounds validation. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix for this vulnerability is not yet in this function.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix not checking for maximum number of DCID

When receiving L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ the remo
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7cf3b1dd6aa603fd80969e9e7160becf1455a0eb
Author: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Date:   Mon Mar 15 13:04:37 2021 -0700

    Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix not checking for maximum number of DCID
    
    When receiving L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ the remote may request
    more channels than allowed by the spec (10 octecs = 5 CIDs) so this
    checks if the number of channels is bigger than the maximum allowed and
    respond with an error.
    
    Signed-off-by: Luiz Aug
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the key logic in l2cap_ecred_conn_req() around deriving num_scid from cmd_len and validating it before any use of the fixed-size response buffer. In this commit, the code computes the number of requested CIDs early: "cmd_len -= sizeof(*req); num_scid = cmd_len / sizeof(u16);" and then immediately validates it with "if (num_scid > ARRAY_SIZE(pdu.dcid)) { result = L2CAP_CR_LE_INVALID_PARAMS; goto response; }". The response buffer is a fixed stack object with DCID array "__le16 dcid[L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID];", and the new check ensures attacker-controlled cmd_len cannot imply more CIDs than the buffer can hold. This is exactly the missing validation described in the root cause. Also, the old placement of "cmd_len -= sizeof(*req); num_scid = cmd_len / sizeof(u16);" after setting success was removed, showing the fix moved validation before later processing/response sizing. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.
